# ADR 0003: Deterministic scenario-probability engine

- Status: proposed implementation
- Date: 2026-08-08
- Scope: public Probability Machine research preview

## Decision

Matrix Reprogrammed will publish scenario probabilities only when a natural-language question has been compiled into a measurable proposition with a jurisdiction, horizon and resolution rule. The first supported family is `surveillance_state`, resolved when at least six of nine published threshold conditions persist for twelve consecutive months.

The headline percentage is generated by deterministic code. A language model may later retrieve, classify or explain evidence, but it may not directly choose the published probability. The engine combines a horizon-adjusted prior, structural signals, evidence likelihood updates, institutional counterweights and an interaction model in log-odds space. It publishes a central estimate, uncertainty range, confidence, component disagreement, drivers, counter-drivers, missing evidence, falsifiers, model version and deterministic run identifier.

## Proprietary boundary

The public repository contains the reproducible calculation contract and a deliberately generic, low-confidence fallback. Jurisdiction-specific priors, signal profiles, model weights and calibration strength are loaded from the private Cloudflare runtime binding `PROBABILITY_MODEL_CONFIG_JSON`. Unknown, malformed or absent private configuration fails back to the generic public seed rather than exposing secrets or fabricating specificity.

## Evidence and safety boundaries

- Risk-clock pressure indices are not relabelled as event probabilities.
- Forecasts do not prove intent, guilt, coordination or inevitability.
- Duplicate evidence is suppressed by independence group.
- The public endpoint is stateless in this phase, does not mutate D1 and makes no external provider call.
- Request size, evidence count, horizon and supported-family limits fail closed.
- Production calibration is not claimed until resolved outcomes support Brier score, log loss and reliability reporting.

## Consequences

The first release is useful as a transparent forecasting interface and integration contract, but its generic public fallback is intentionally low confidence. Accuracy improvement requires a private evidence-to-signal pipeline, historical analogue data, a forecast-resolution ledger and repeated calibration against outcomes. A later ADR will govern persistent forecast storage and automated evidence updates before those features are enabled.
